title: De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory for kinetic equations with nonlocal diffusions: mixed-norm estimates for the kinetic parametrix
author: Francesca Anceschi, Giampiero Palatucci, Mirco Piccinini
work: De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory for kinetic equations with nonlocal diffusions
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem (source0.tex lines 917--941, source label sharp:thm_mixed_parametrix), presented in the article as "our main result" in the section on sharp estimates for the kinetic parametrix: three mixed-norm bounds for the parametrix operator, namely a bound on the mixed Lebesgue space with velocity component in the square-integrable scale for sources in the corresponding mixed space, the same bound with a fractional velocity derivative applied to the source, and a bound in the full mixed space for exponents above the threshold; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 942--1017 (one adjacent proof environment of 76 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span together with its retained context. It first reduces to smooth compactly supported sources and proves each of the three estimates in turn: it applies the retained fixed-parameter proposition with the critical exponents and evaluates the resulting time convolution, it verifies the scaling identities that make the convolved kernel integrable, it introduces the intermediate exponents for the third estimate, applies the retained scalar estimate, computes the two scaling identities relating those exponents, and then invokes the retained Hardy--Littlewood--Stein inequality with the correct exponent to close the estimate, finally extending all three bounds to the stated source spaces by density. Every quoted input is delivered as a retained labelled display or as the statement of a retained proposition, and the article's own exponents and homogeneous dimensions are used exactly as printed. H2: a research-level harmonic-analysis theorem on mixed-norm smoothing estimates for a kinetic parametrix with fractional velocity diffusion; the combination of critical exponents, convolution in time, scaling identities and the Stein interpolation inequality is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
